content:
jamie: heads up — eval CI canary failed on redwood-mini-3b-quant. metric_agreement dropped ~8 points on legalqa and contract_qa.
olga: ouch. is this the new quant build or a runner change? :thinking_face:
simon: link to the failing report?
ci-bot: <https://ci.internal/reports/ci-1719001234> — job 402: eval-canary/redwood-mini-3b-quant
jamie: report attached. summary: baseline 0.82 -> 0.74 on metric_agreement across canonical prompts. variance small, not flaky.
nancy: tagging @simon @kevin — this is a release blocker for the quant rollout.
kevin: do we have a suspect range? when did metrics start drifting?
jamie: first appeared in yesterday's night canary (around 1718920000). last good run was 1718830000. suspect window: 1718830000..1718920000.
simon: ok can we bisect quickly on the eval-runner image + tokenizer artifacts. two suspects: runner/trim-padding change (merged 1718854000) and tokenizer/normalize-whitespace (merged 1718885000).
nancy: i'll run a narrow bisect: pin runner image to before/after and run the legalqa eval locally.
runner-bot: kicked off local job: eval-local/1719001248 (status: running)
jamie: logs show answers differ in subtle trailing-space retention. example: expected "Section 2.1" got "Section\u00A0 2.1" (non-breaking space).
kevin: that smells like tokenizer normalization.
nancy: quick results — runner pinned to pre-1718854000 still fails. runner pinned to post-1718854000 and pre-1718885000 still fails. when I pin tokenizer to pre-1718885000 metrics return to baseline.
simon: so tokenizer/normalize-whitespace is the likely culprit. can you paste the git range you tested?
nancy: tested tokenizer at commit range: 1718879001..1718886000. bisect midpoint 1718884500 (normalize whitespace PR landed there).
ci-bot: failing test excerpt:
```
metric_agreement: baseline 0.82 -> current 0.74
example id 4821
expected: "The tenant shall pay rent"
actual  : "The tenant\u00A0shall pay rent"
``` 
jamie: the NBSP is causing downstream exact-match-based agreement scoring to fail. our metric_agreement uses normalized whitespace but apparently not NBSP.
kevin: why didn't unit tests catch this? tokenizer tests only check ASCII spaces.
simon: we added a change to Unicode normalization to preserve NBSP in tokenizer output (intentional) but eval metrics expect collapsing of all spacing variants. mismatch of assumptions.
olga: options: revert tokenizer change, update metric normalizer to map NBSP->space, or update eval harness to normalize more aggressively. what's least risky short-term?
nancy: short-term: pin the tokenizer wheel in the canary image to pre-1718884500. medium-term: patch metric normalizer to normalize all Unicode space categories.
jamie: agree. we should pin in CI and hold the quant rollout until we ship a metrics-fix. make a quick PR to metric normalizer and a follow-up to reintroduce tokenizer change intentionally with tests.
kevin: I'll cut a canary pin PR and a bugfix PR for the eval-harness normalizer. tagging infra for image rebuild.
kevin: PRs: <https://git.internal/r/infra/ci-pin-tokenizer/6> and <https://git.internal/r/eval/normalize-unicode-space/12>
runner-bot: created canary image with pinned tokenizer: gcr.internal/redwood-eval:ci-pin-1718879000
nancy: reran canary with pinned tokenizer — metric_agreement back to 0.81. passing. build 417.
jamie: ok blocking decision: pin tokenizer in CI (merged), hold rollout. follow-up: update eval-harness normalizer and add regression test with NBSP to prevent recurrence.
olga: can we add a quick eval-case with NBSP/ZWSP/regular-space variants in the test suite? would catch future tokenizer changes.
simon: will add tests to eval-harness and add a gating check in CI.
jamie: great. documenting here for release notes and postmortem. thanks everyone :pray:
ci-bot: note: release unblocked once eval-harness PR merged and canary stable for 3 runs.
kevin: assigning follow-ups: @simon (add tests + normalizer PR), @nancy (verify canary + update runbook), @kevin (image pin + release hold).
nancy: copying to #incidents for tracking. closing thread after follow-ups merged.
